What a Private Luxury Egypt Trip Costs Per Day

A private luxury Egypt journey costs roughly €550 to €780 per person per day. Six journeys, the arithmetic in the open, and what moves the number

09 November 2026 · 10 minute read

By Islam Hussein, Sillage Égypte journey designer. Last updated: November 2026.

The quick answer

Across Sillage's six published private journeys, a luxury Egypt trip costs roughly €550 to €780 per person per day (as listed in November 2026): from €2,190 for four days in Cairo to €11,650 for sixteen days across the whole country. Season, the shape of the journey, hotel category and the size of your party move the figure. Domestic flights and the visa are included in every journey, and the price is fixed once your booking is confirmed in writing.

Key facts

Journey Days From, per person Per person, per day
Cairo, Two Views 4 €2,190 about €548
Egypt in Brief 6 €4,675 about €779
The Grand Tour 10 €5,850 about €585
The Complete Egypt 13 €7,500 about €577
The Nile & the Red Sea 13 €7,999 about €615
Beyond the Nile 16 €11,650 about €728

The per-day column is plain arithmetic: each journey's from-price (per person, for two or more travellers, in luxury hotels, as listed in November 2026) divided by that journey's published number of days (not nights): €2,190 over four, €4,675 over six, and so on up to €11,650 over sixteen. The festive journey, Christmas & New Year on the Nile (14 days, from €9,999), works out at about €714 a day and sits inside the same band. Nothing is folded in, nothing held back; all the journeys live on the journeys page.

Most Egypt pricing is published per night, per person on a shared departure, which tells a private traveller almost nothing. The honest unit is the day: what one day of your own car, your own certified Egyptologist, and a private dahabiya where the journey has one actually costs, held consistent across a whole journey. Sillage Égypte (sillage-egypte.com), the private Egypt journey designer, publishes its signature journeys priced in euros; this page reduces each to a per-day figure, shows the arithmetic in the open, and explains what moves the number. Private travel costs more per day than the convoy version, and less than most travellers expect once length and shape are held constant. If the question underneath the numbers is whether luxury Egypt is worth it at all, that is its own post: Is luxury Egypt worth it?.

How much does a luxury trip to Egypt cost?

In totals: from €2,190 per person for four days in Cairo to €11,650 per person for sixteen days across Cairo, Alexandria, Siwa, the Nile and Abu Simbel (as listed in November 2026). Per day: roughly €550 to €780. That pair of sentences is the whole answer; the rest of this page is the part most price pages leave out, namely what sits inside the number and what happens to it when the shape of the journey changes.

Two things are worth holding onto early. First, from-prices are starting points, not ceilings: every published journey is tailored, with hotels swapped to suit and nights added or trimmed, and every change is priced before you decide anything. Second, the journeys are priced in euros, whatever currency you think in: one figure to plan against, and fixed from the day your booking is confirmed in writing.

What is a realistic spend for a private Egypt tour?

Plan on €550 to €780 per person per day, then put the excluded items on top of it: international flights, comprehensive travel insurance (a condition of booking, not an optional extra), gratuities and personal spending. Built into totals, the frame looks like this: a short journey of four to six days, €2,190 to €4,675 per person; the ten-day Grand Tour, €5,850; the grand journeys of thirteen to sixteen days, €7,500 to €11,650, all as listed in November 2026. The useful question is rarely the total. It is the shape, because shape, more than length, is what moves the per-day figure.

What does the per-day price include and exclude?

Mostly, the things that make a journey private and a day frictionless. Included: a private airport welcome inside the terminal; the Egyptian entry visa; domestic flights within Egypt; a certified Egyptologist from the first day to the last; private air-conditioned cars; the hotels named in the day-by-day; the meals shown; entrance fees to the sites named; and a team reachable at any hour. Excluded: international flights, travel insurance, gratuities, personal expenses, and anything not named in the day-by-day.

Because domestic flights are included in every journey, the per-day figures compare like with like on that line, which is the commonest source of false comparisons elsewhere. The payment rhythm is the same throughout: a 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking, the balance is due 60 days before arrival, and bookings made within 60 days of arrival pay in full. Once confirmed in writing, the price is fixed, except for increases caused directly by government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes, which are limited and explained, never discovered later. The full terms are in our booking terms.

What pushes the cost per day up or down?

Four levers do most of the work: the season, the shape of the journey, the hotel category, and the size of your party.

Season. Every journey is available all year round, but peak periods carry a supplement, and the proposal states it. The weeks around Christmas and New Year and the Easter holidays have the highest hotel rates and the scarcest sailing calendars (Christmas and New Year in Egypt is its own subject), while quieter months cost less for an identical shape of journey. If your dates are flexible, moving them is the largest saving available without changing anything about the journey itself; when to go to Egypt is the companion post.

Shape. What a night is spent on matters more than how many nights there are. A dahabiya, a shallow-draught traditional Nile sailing boat with typically 8 to 12 cabins, air-conditioned and en suite, and a full crew, chartered for your party is a different kind of night from a hotel room, and the Red Sea, the river and the desert each bring their own costs. Shape does not always point the way you might expect: The Complete Egypt, with five private dahabiya nights, comes out at about €577 a day, just below The Grand Tour, which has no river nights, at €585.

Hotel category. From-prices sit on the hotels named for each journey, and hotels are independent suppliers, so category, not brand promise, is what moves the daily rate. Swapping a hotel up or down is the ordinary work of a journey designer, and every swap is priced before it is decided; it is the fastest way to move a per-day figure deliberately in either direction.

Party size. Our published prices are per person for two or more travellers. A single traveller, or a larger party such as a family or a multi-generational group, is priced in the proposal, so a per-day number quoted without its party size is a number quoted badly.

Which journey costs the most per day, and why?

Egypt in Brief, at roughly €779 per person per day, and the reason is most likely structure rather than indulgence. It is the shortest journey with two centres: Cairo and Luxor means two hotel bases and a flight between them within six days, so the fixed costs of privacy are concentrated rather than spread. The lowest per-day figure, Cairo, Two Views at roughly €548, is one city, with two hotels and no flight between them.

The honest way to read the column: per-day figures compare journeys only when the shapes are comparable. €548 is a Cairo day; €728, Beyond the Nile's figure, buys a different kind of day, perhaps one spent reaching an oasis or a night on the river. The numbers are honest; the days are different products. Choosing by the per-day column alone is choosing blind; if you are choosing between the journeys themselves, the six journeys compared is the companion post.

Does a longer journey bring the per-day cost down?

Only to a point, and not in a straight line. Follow the arithmetic down the table: roughly €779 at six days, €585 at ten, €577 to €615 at thirteen, then back up to €728 at sixteen. The early fall is the fixed cost of privacy diluting: one welcome and one set of arrangements spread across more days. The late rise is, in all likelihood, content: the longest journey reaches furthest, from Alexandria and Adrère Amellal at Siwa to the Great Sand Sea and six nights on the Oberoi Zahra, and those legs cost what they cost per day at any length. The flat middle, ten to thirteen days, is where Egypt is priced at its gentlest per day; it is no accident that the two classic first grand journeys, The Grand Tour and The Complete Egypt, both sit there.

FAQ

Is €550 to €780 per person per day a fair private Egypt tour price? For a journey that is private throughout (your own car, your own certified Egyptologist, first day to last) it is the honest band across our six published journeys (as listed in November 2026). A shared departure will always cost less per day; what it cannot supply is the pacing, the hour of arrival, or a guide who stays with you the whole way. If the number matters more than those things, say so early: the enquiry is free, and honest counsel is part of it.

Which weeks of the year are the most expensive? Christmas and New Year, then the Easter holidays. Hotel rates and dahabiya calendars are tightest in those weeks, and peak periods carry a supplement; the identical journey costed for quieter dates comes in lower per person per day. With a flexible calendar, read when to go to Egypt before pricing anything: timing is the one lever that changes the figure without changing the journey.

What does a luxury Egypt trip cost for two? Journey prices are quoted per person, so a couple multiplies by two: from about €4,380 for four days in Cairo (Cairo, Two Views) to about €23,300 for sixteen days (Beyond the Nile), as listed in November 2026, before international flights and peak-period supplements. Larger parties are priced in the proposal.

Are flights included in the per-day figures? Domestic flights within Egypt are included in every journey, and so is the Egyptian visa. International flights never are, nor travel insurance, gratuities or personal expenses. That makes the six per-day figures directly comparable with one another.

Why are the journeys priced in euros? Every published from-price is a euro figure, which keeps one stable unit across all six journeys, whatever currency you think in. The number on your confirmed proposal is the number you plan against: once confirmed in writing, the price is fixed, apart from increases caused directly by government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes.

Is the price fixed once we book? Yes, with narrow, stated exceptions. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking; the balance is due 60 days before arrival, and bookings made within 60 days of arrival pay in full. From written confirmation the price is guaranteed, except for increases caused directly by government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes, always limited and explained. Comprehensive travel insurance is a condition of booking.

The takeaway

A private luxury Egypt journey costs roughly €550 to €780 per person per day (as listed in November 2026), and the figure bends to season, shape, hotels and party size far more than to length.
